solution: Any operation sequence for one value can be normalized to some number of halvings followed by doublings, because every adjacent double-then-half pair cancels. Enumerate every positive value floor(x / 2^a) * 2^b that is at most sum, assigning it cost a + b. Then use a multiple-choice 0/1 knapsack DP where dp[t] stores the minimum cost to obtain subset sum t, processing each original element once. This is correct because the enumeration covers every useful reachable value and the DP considers exactly the possible subset choices; its complexity is O(n · sum · log(max(nums)) · log(sum)) time and O(sum) space. It produces 3, 2, and -1 for the three worked examples.
